publicExactCheckpointBody:
## Autonomous roadmap checkpoint — held at explicit owner gates

Six of twenty issues remain locally accepted: #2, #3, #5, #6, #8 and #11. No additional feature was accepted in this review cycle. The full roadmap, eighty acceptance criteria, five milestones and forty-one native dependencies remain in scope; I have not changed assignees or milestone dates.

- **#7 read model:** the third authorized prospective repair/review cycle is complete, but both independent reviews remain FIX-FIRST. Their conservative union has four HIGH finding families: whole-JSON completeness, strict supported UTF-8 handling, publication of the captured primary result before the hard deadline, and preservation of the earliest failure identity. The authorized three-cycle budget is exhausted. No extra cycle, source application or runtime activation is authorized automatically.
- **#4 DSH integration:** the complete design repair received an original-review SHIP for the proposal only and an independent-quality FIX-FIRST with one HIGH ownership gap covering private model-iterator cleanup and detached tool-result callbacks. Both reviews computed the same proposal digest. Both actual native Done messages and reviewer releases were observed; the disagreement is preserved for human resolution. The design repair counter remains 1/2. All four original runtime criteria remain unaccepted.
- **Orchestration:** the demonstrated Orca runtime metadata failure was recovered through its documented native startup path. The original read-model author remains positively observed live and retains sole ownership; no replacement author or retry was created.

Next owner decisions: whether to authorize one additional bounded prospective #7 cycle, and whether to resolve the #4 disagreement by authorizing the remaining DESIGN-only repair. Neither choice grants implementation, runtime or paid-provider authority. No model-generation calls have been made. The coordinator continues to avoid direct production, test, dataset and SDK code work.

This is a blocked delivery checkpoint, not completion, feature acceptance, a merge-ready claim or a reduction of the roadmap.
